tools.description: When was this chain last anchored off-box, and does the local chain still match it? Returns the latest anchor (range, status, events since), and a verification of that range: the local Merkle root recomputed and compared with the anchored root (match | diverged | beyond_head | gap), plus the service countersignature checked with cached keys. remote:true also asks the service (conflict flag, fresh keys); an unreachable service is reported, never an error. diverged means the local chain was rewritten after it was anchored.

result.description: Local root over the last anchored range vs the anchored root.

tools.title: Hosted anchor status

tools.description: The reconciliation surface. Pass the facts you are about to act on as claims {symbol, value}: symbol is a block id (value = its content or content_hash), a document slug (value = revision number, markdown hash, or markdown), or "head" (value = chain seq or hash). Each claim is graded current | stale (a newer version exists) | contradicted (the live value differs) | retracted (tombstoned) | unknown, with the current truth and a reconcile line. Use it after a drift banner or retraction list, before writing.

tools.description: Compute a Merkle root over event hashes in [from_seq, to_seq] (default: 1..head), sign it with the server key, and store it. verify_chain checks checkpoints. push:true also sends the signed root (never the events) to the hosted anchor service configured in the data dir and stores its countersigned receipt; the result's anchor object says whether that worked. The local checkpoint is stored even when the service is unreachable.

push.description: Also anchor the checkpoint off-box (leaves the machine: root, range, signature, public key).

conflict.description: This range was anchored earlier with a different root: the chain was rewritten.

duplicate.description: Same checkpoint was anchored before; the original receipt is returned.

error.description: Why the push did not complete. The local checkpoint is stored either way.

ok.description: true when the service countersigned and the receipt verified.

tools.description: Orient call — INSTRUCTS the agent. Call at session start AND before any write-class work. Present your previous `cursor` (or `cursor_compact`) as `since_cursor` to get a true delta: cold start receives the digest plus everything; warm wake receives only what changed since your cursor. Honor the drift banner: when it is surfaced, your memory of this store is stale and the delta is the catch-up. When retractions are reported, reconcile BEFORE acting — affirm the current truth (cite seq), name the old claim once, stop using it as a premise. An invalid or missing cursor never fails: position is recovered from the flight recorder or genesis, and the response says which. Focuses: orientation (default: digest + delta + retractions) | recent_changes (delta + retractions) | retractions (only retractions) | pulse (head + drift banner, ~50 tokens; call this before every write and only pay for a full delta when the banner surfaces). response_format markdown (default) or json controls the text block; structuredContent always carries the JSON state. Always carry the returned cursor forward.

tools.description: Store a Markdown document under a slug. A new slug creates revision 1; an existing slug creates the next revision: unchanged blocks keep their ids, changed blocks are superseded (old → new), removed blocks are tombstoned. Emits document.put + block.* events and returns every block id with its BLAKE3 content hash and the new chain head. Pass your cursor so the response can tell you if you are writing on stale assumptions (advisory only).

tools.description: Full-text search (bm25) over live document blocks. Each hit carries a signed receipt v2 binding (block_id, content_hash, doc_slug, revision) to the chain head at issue time. Keep the receipt with any claim you derive from the block; pass it to verify() later to learn whether the block is still current (VERIFIED), was replaced (SUPERSEDED, with the current head), was retired (TOMBSTONED), or cannot be trusted (UNVERIFIED). Superseded blocks are never returned; tombstoned only with include_tombstoned. Set include_receipts:false for a lean result.

tools.description: Replace a live block's content with a new block (old → new supersession, with a reason). Receipts issued for the old block will verify as SUPERSEDED pointing at the new one. The document gets a new revision. Refused if the block is already superseded or tombstoned (operate on the current head instead).

tools.description: Re-derive a receipt against the live store. Fail-closed. Checks the Ed25519 signature (local key registry), block existence, content hash, that the receipt's chain position is still on the chain, and walks supersession to the current head. Returns VERIFIED | SUPERSEDED (with current_block_id/current_content_hash) | TOMBSTONED | UNVERIFIED with a closed-enum reason. Malformed input yields UNVERIFIED/malformed_receipt, never a tool error.
